title: Mega Man Powered Up
subtitle: The first Mega Man becomes a toy box
summary: Mega Man Powered Up is Capcom's PSP platform game, first released in Japan on 2 March 2006. body: Mega Man Powered Up is Capcom's PSP platform game, first released in Japan on 2 March 2006. It rebuilds the 1987 Mega Man with rounded three-dimensional characters, new stages and additional playable Robot Masters. The familiar campaign still asks Mega Man to defeat Dr. Wily's machines and use their powers, but the remake enlarges what can be done with that foundation. A level editor and challenge mode turn the original's rules into tools for further play. Its small, expressive figures make the adventure look approachable even when the platforming demands careful control.

Under the right conditions, Robot Masters can be unlocked as playable characters. Each brings a different ability into spaces originally approached with Mega Man's more general movement and attacks. A familiar obstacle may become easier, stranger or require a new route because the controlled character has changed. This gives the roster a practical role beyond the boss encounters. The player learns not only which weapon works against another machine, but how the whole platforming system feels when one of those specialised machines is responsible for completing the stage.

The editor allows original levels to be constructed from the game's components, extending play beyond the supplied campaign. Challenge mode adds another set of focused tasks. Kazuki Matsue directed the project and Toshihiko Horiyama composed the music. Its compact character style reflected ideas that could not be realised in the same way on the original NES hardware. Reviews were positive, but weak sales ended plans for a similar Mega Man 2 remake. Powered Up remains a particularly expansive revisit, using the first game's machinery as the basis for both a campaign and a creative toolkit.
